rationale: Ground truth has no substantive concerns to recall, so both score trivially high there; the split comes down to finding quality. Both independently catch the same highest-value bug (the new test lacks pytestmark and is deselected by the CI marker filter, so the regression guard never runs) and both flag the same doc/pyproject 'Blackwell' wording drift. Y goes further with two novel, well-grounded functional findings X misses entirely: warmup_quack_fp8() bypasses quack_enabled() and can raise on sm_120 during the documented build-time warmup, and warning_once keys on the exception object so the flood-log symptom isn't actually deduped — both cite exact lines and are directly relevant to the bug this PR fixes. X's extra findings (sm_110 ambiguity, pyproject comment, kernel-load test gap) are valid but skew toward minor/doc nits already partially echoed by Y. X's GitHub-suggestion-block formatting is marginally more machine-actionable, keeping the margin slight rather than clear.
